items.title: UBS acquires 4.8% stake in 360 ONE WAM: What the warrant conversion means for India's wealth market - Decoded
paras: The warrants were allotted on July 21, 2025, with 25% of the exercise price paid at the time of allotment. UBS AG has now exercised all the warrants and paid the remaining 75% of the exercise price.

“Pursuant to this, 360 ONE has allotted 2,05,02,939 equity shares to UBS AG, representing approximately a 4.8% equity stake in 360 ONE WAM Ltd,” the company said in a regulatory filing. The move comes as global private banks face increasing competition from domestic players, including Kotak Mahindra Bank’s private banking arm and 360 ONE.

India is among the world’s fastest-growing wealth markets, with nearly a million millionaires and at least 211 billionaires, according to UBS estimates. In April 2025, the companies announced a partnership under which UBS agreed to sell its Indian onshore wealth management business to 360 ONE for around $32 million, while acquiring warrants representing a 4.95% stake in the Indian firm.

items.title: Rubio turns to small Indian town as US faces high oil prices
paras: The western Indian port town of Jamnagar is not a usual stop for foreign leaders, yet it featured prominently in US Secretary of State Marco Rubio's recent visit. And, more importantly, why did he skip the Indian capital, Delhi?

The answer to both questions may have less to do with India and more to do with Donald Trump administration's domestic compulsions – or, more precisely, its domestic oil needs. Rubio arrived in the financial capital Mumbai on Tuesday, where he met Indian Foreign Minister S Jaishankar and some of the country's top business leaders.

He officially ended his trip in Jamnagar - in the western state of Gujarat - home to the giant oil refinery owned by one of Asia's richest men, Mukesh Ambani. It was his second trip to the country this year and experts say what is significant this time is the timing of the visit as well as his choice of destinations.

items.title: Former Grand Slam champion set to drop 60 places in the rankings and fall outside the top 180 in the world now
paras: Kenin is a Grand Slam champion, having won the Australian Open in 2020 after beating the likes of Coco Gauff , Ash Barty and Garbine Muguruza to claim the title. Prior to the Australian Open that year, Kenin had not even reached the quarter-finals of a major tournament before, but she would then go on to reach another Grand Slam final later that year at Roland Garros.
Kenin has been ranked as high as world number four, but she is now far from that ranking after a string of poor results. Who is the most shocking Grand Slam champion ever?

Kenin began the 2026 season ranked as the world number 28, having reached the final of the Charleston Open and the semi-finals of the Tokyo Open last year. The American has been unable to even reach a quarter-final this year, with Kenin winning just eight of her 33 matches this year.

items.title: WTA Osaka Semifinal Predictions Including Ann Li vs Ashlyn Krueger
paras: As always, we here at LWOT will be offering our predictions for every match on the slate, as well as all the action at WTA Ningbo, but who will book their spot in Sunday’s final?
Both Ann Li and Ashlyn Krueger will surely be coming into this match with real confidence after impressive weeks so far at WTA Osaka.

Li, the top seed in Japan, opened her campaign by battling past Emerson Jones from a set down, but she backed that up with a more assured performance in the second round against Zeynep Sonmez, winning 6-3 6-1. Li was then pushed hard in the quarterfinals by Lili Tagger, but came out on top by winning a final-set tiebreak 7-0. Krueger, meanwhile, has not yet dropped a set at WTA Osaka, beating sixth seed Janice Tjen, Lana Tararudee, and then fourth seed Talia Gibson – all in fairly comprehensive fashion – to reach the last four.

items.title: ‘Staying healthy is a real skill’: Mouratoglou explains why Zverev deserves to be No. 1
paras: Patrick Mouratoglou believes Alexander Zverev fully deserves his No. 1 ranking, even if Jannik Sinner and Carlos Alcaraz are better players.

Staying healthy, he argues, is “a real skill” that demands sacrifice, and Zverev’s two Grand Slam titles in 2026 marked a mental breakthrough. Alexander Zverev may not be the best player in the world, but his ranking is fully deserved.

That is Patrick Mouratoglou’s view, set out in a video on his social media channels in which he argued that staying healthy is a skill in itself, and part of a player’s value. “Zverev might not be the best player, but he’s the number one in the world, and he fully deserves it,” Mouratoglou said. “The first way I read the situation is that your ranking is your value.

items.title: Stefanos Tsitsipas reacts to Gael Monfils suddenly retiring from tennis, ‘I’m actually quite sad’
paras: Gael Monfils’ retirement from tennis is a huge shame, but it did feel inevitable. After all, at 40 years of age, the French magician had given plenty to the sport across a sparkling 22-year career.

He has earned the right to depart on his own terms, still proving himself more than competitive at the pinnacle. It’s desperately sad that he will not get the dramatic send-off that a player of his calibre deserves, having opted against playing in Lyon and Paris.

Stefanos Tsitsipas is the latest to weigh in on the legendary veteran’s departure from the sport, speaking after his latest win in Kazakhstan. He continued: “I’m actually quite sad that tennis is going to lose a person like that. You don’t find players on tour like him, and I really don’t know when it’s going to be the next one, his predecessor, because he just has this charisma about himself that it’s very difficult to find another person.”

Friendships are built by repeated contact, not by being liked
items.hook: This is the single most useful fact in the whole guide.
paras: Studies of primary-school classrooms found that children seated next to each other were far more likely to become friends than children seated across the room. When teachers changed the seating, new friendships formed with the new neighbours.

So the engine is: same place, same people, same activity, over and over. The day at the yo-yo bar followed by basketball is that engine working - shared activity changed how the other boy treated him. It was not luck.
items.do: Pick one activity he already likes and commit to it weekly for a full term.

items.title: Keep the proximity - change the watching
items.hook: Your instinct is half right, and the other half matters.
paras: You are right that being around the group matters: children nominate as friends the children they see and interact with most. 'Out of sight, out of mind' is real for acquaintances.

But guidance written for schools is blunt: merely remaining beside a group is not friendship. A child who hovers is read as a bystander rather than a player, and it holds him in the one-down position. Watching has a use - but only as the first twenty seconds of joining in, never as the endpoint.
items.do: Keep telling him to stay near the group. Add: 'then take a job in the game'.

items.title: Teach 'watch, then blend'
items.hook: The best way to join a game is not to ask.
paras: Most of us were told to walk up and say 'Can I play?' But that makes everyone stop and look at him, and makes 'no' very easy.

The better sequence, used by people who study play: watch for about twenty seconds to learn the game and where the line is, then slide into the action without stopping it. Take the end of the line. Stand in the outfield. Pick up the ball and pass it back.
items.do: Rehearse it at home in five minutes. Ask him to name the 'easiest job' in each game.

items.title: Host one friend at a time - this is the biggest lever you control
items.hook: The child who invites is rarely short of friends.
paras: Pick a child he has had fun with in the last month, not someone he admires from afar. Invite one person for one to two hours. Put away anything precious, have two activities ready, start with a snack, and let the guest choose sometimes.
Keep it short and end while they are both still enjoying it. Then leave a few weeks before inviting the same child again, so the invitation can come back to him.
items.do: Text one parent this week and set a date for the school holidays.

items.title: Ask the teacher one specific question
items.hook: Teachers see the playground. Ask them to name names.
paras: Ask two things: who does he play well with, and could he be seated near them or paired with them for group work?
Seating is one of the few levers that reliably creates new friendships, and it is invisible to the children - no one has to know it was arranged.
items.do: Email the teacher this week with those two questions.

items.title: Do not push into a group that is rejecting him
items.hook: Here the advice is the opposite of persistence.
paras: Where a group is actively excluding him, the guidance is to back off - when you back off from people, they can move towards you. Put his energy into two or three other children instead of one closed circle.
Friends in more than one place - school, a club, family friends - also make him far less vulnerable when one group turns cold.
items.do: Help him list three children outside the difficult group he could get to know.

items.title: One or two good friends is the goal - not popularity
paras: Kids need one or two good friends. You do not need to worry about him being the most popular child in the class.
His warmth and kindness are already the raw material. Treat this as coaching a skill, not fixing a fault - if he feels like a project, he will resist.
items.do: Say his strengths out loud, often. Confidence is what carries a child into a group.

items.title: Playing and talking with girls is normal and good
items.hook: Children believe gender matters far more than it actually does.
paras: In one large classroom experiment, simply seating boys and girls next to each other doubled how often they became friends.
Girls' play tends to build conversation, turn-taking and inventing games together; boys' play builds bigger, faster group play. Being good at both widens his circle.
items.do: No action needed. Just do not let him think it is odd.

items.title: When to get more help
items.hook: Ordinary friendship difficulty is not a disorder.
paras: Get more support if he becomes reluctant to go to school, is persistently distressed, has changes in sleep or appetite, or says it is happening all the time and he cannot make it stop.
Start with his teacher, then the school counsellor, then your GP for a referral. Kids Helpline is free and open 24/7 on 1800 55 1800, for children and for parents.
items.do: Save Kids Helpline in your phone: 1800 55 1800.
